note: Ship console Field guide: 7's short observations of the people and creatures she has met, only from what the story has shown. titleBefore/textBefore are used until nameUnlock is met (the cat is "The cat" until VEN_B01). portrait = image key (cat, scree, elarim_guardian, elarim_attendant, elarim, worm, wormmaster, tunneler, ratwing). Unlock forms: "ch1>=N" (Chapter 1 checkpoint N reached: 0 cell, 1 escape, 2 old passage + ruins, 3 Scree guard, 4 vision, 5 lunar door + take the shape, 6 city reveal, 7 saucer rescue + beam, 8 aboard, 9 galley, 10 free exploration), "venus>=<Stage>" (Landed, GuardianMet, HelpAccepted, ControlDiscovered, EncounterActive, ThreatStopped, RecordReceived, Complete), "scene:<VEN scene id>" (that Venus scene completed), "europa>=N" (Europa checkpoint N), or "never". QF13: an entry grows with the story - optional "more": [{"text", "unlock"}] paragraphs are shown after the main text, each only once its unlock is met (never mention a place or event the player has not reached). entries.title: Panther
entries.textBefore: A black cat who speaks in my head, only conversationally. His people sent him to get me out of the prison; they did not tell him why, and he came anyway. He has views on chicken: free-range only.
entries.text: His name is Panther. He can grow from house-cat size to something very large, smoothly, in the middle of a stretch. He doesn’t see what I see, so I tell him when I get back. He chose to stay.

entries.title: The Scree
entries.text: Tall, armored people who guard the Moon prison; some of them were working rather than watching. I got past them without hurting anyone. The two on the terrace went down and sat up again afterwards. I don’t know yet whether any of them chose this.

more.text: On Europa they laboured in Tunneler’s underwater base until the doors were open - then they opened doors themselves and showed me the safe routes.

entries.title: The guardian
entries.text: Keeper of the Elarim temple on Venus and its cube. Asked to see the shape before anything else, and listened to all of it.

more.text: Asked me to remember that the creatures were being driven.
Gave me a copy of their record; the original stays in the temple.

entries.title: The attendant
entries.text: Works at the temple with the guardian. Came into the cube chamber with the news that the lower channel had collapsed.

entries.title: The Elarim
entries.text: The people of the Venus gardens. They tend the terraces and the water channels and keep repairing the ground.

more.text: Their marking is on the shape I found on the Moon.
“Our histories were not always kept apart,” the guardian said.

entries.title: The burrowing creatures
entries.text: Burrowers that live beneath the Venus gardens. They never attacked the people. They were following a signal through the foundations.

more.text: When the devices stopped, they went home, all of them unharmed.

entries.title: The Wormmaster
entries.text: He drove the burrowing creatures with machines from a chamber under the gardens, to force the Elarim to give up their temple. He told me I don’t know what I’m interfering with. He is contained now, not hurt.

entries.title: Tunneler
entries.text: He calls himself Tunneler. He ran the Moon prison I was held in, and the mining that is cutting into the city inside the Moon; the Scree did the work.
entries.textBefore: Someone runs the prison I was held in on the Moon, and the mining that is cutting into the city inside it. The Scree do the work. I never saw who.

more.text: On Europa he spoke to me from a screen in his underwater base: ring-segmented, with a spiral drill for a head that turns when he speaks. His machinery silenced the Cetaceans’ calls, and he worked Scree who could not leave. He promised to take only what nobody would miss.
He escaped in his own craft - and he will remember.

entries.title: Ratwing
entries.text: (Not met yet.)
entries.note: Only in the Round 4 cave demo, not in a chapter. Write the entry and set an unlock when he appears in the story.

entries.title: The Cetaceans
entries.text: Europa’s people live in the ocean under the ice: vast, slow, and they speak - an understandable voice carried on their calls.

more.text: They teach their history through sound, one voice to another.

entries.title: The keeper
entries.text: An ancient Cetacean who keeps the settlement and the old routes. Calm, patient; becomes very still when something does not belong.

more.text: Gave me Europa’s record and asked me to carry it somewhere it can be heard.

entries.title: Reptilians
entries.text: The people of Mars's two kingdoms: workers, families, traders, guards. Ordinary people on both banks of the ravine; their distrust has its reasons.

more.text: Their two kingdoms' symbols turned out to be halves of one design.

entries.title: The checkpoint guard
entries.text: Holds the main crossing on the west bank. He has his orders, and he keeps them.

more.text: Later I saw him talking with the caretaker by the open barrier. Not friends - but working.

entries.title: The worker
entries.text: Was with the stranded supply transport - water filters for the other bank.

more.text: Volunteered to work one of the temple's two controls.
“We were taught it was taken from us.”

entries.titleBefore: A Reptilian on the far bank
entries.title: The caretaker
entries.text: Keeps the approach to the temple on the east bank. Careful, honest about what both sides want.

more.text: Worked the east control while the worker worked the west.

entries.title: Viper
entries.text: Profits from the division between the two kingdoms; tells each bank the other means to seize the temple. He noticed the records I carry.

more.text: Subdued and contained at the temple approach, left for local custody. “They'll turn on each other again.” That is their choice.

entries.title: The Machinist
entries.textBefore: Something in the central hall keeps this city running.
entries.text: The asteroid's last caretaker: a huge articulated machine with a slit visor and a heavy tool arm. Deliberate, economical, certain. He keeps the city ready for its people's return.

more.text: Immobilized in his own maintenance cradle, then released once he accepted a different instruction: keep what is left safe. The records. The things they made.

entries.title: The Machinists
entries.text: The people of the Great Machine Age. Their workstations stand empty; stools, lockers, a small repaired bird. Nobody has found them yet.

more.text: In the memory the rune held, they stopped a great production line to mend a little bird. They were allowed to. It belonged to them.

entries.title: The city in the asteroid
entries.text: Foundries, transport tunnels, rail carriers and enormous moving assemblies, with a temple built into the central engine. Recycling the archive kept it running.

more.text: Preservation mode: production stopped, the stabilizers and the essential lights kept. The surviving archive panels are in protected storage.

entries.title: The mechanical bird
entries.text: A small wind-up bird; one wing repaired several times with mismatched pieces. Wound, it gives one uneven chirp and flaps a wing.

entries.title: The Biavian mothership
entries.text: An egg-shaped vessel twenty-six miles across, stationed in the rings of Veyra, its hull a luminous pearl-white. A sister ship: the Biavians' main mothership lies in the rings of Saturn. A whole city curves up the inside of its shell - gardens, bridges, transit lights in the mist.

entries.title: The Biavians
entries.text: A people who share their thoughts across the whole ship - and who know how to share only what they choose. The medallion each of them wears carries a mark of its own.

entries.title: Nela
entries.text: The Biavian who welcomed us at the iris and guided me to the relays. Her voice arrives before her. She asks before she shares anything.

entries.title: Ratwing
entries.text: Sly, winged, and very sure of his price. He meant to hold the Biavian archive and sell its own memories back to them. He works alone.

entries.title: The octahedron
entries.text: The mothership's key: eight triangular faces. It holds the memories people chose to leave with the archive.

entries.title: Cattalus
entries.text: Panther's homeworld. Cardboard mansions, cat-tree apartments, carefully occupied patches of sunlight. A gate open is not an invitation to go through.

entries.title: Juniper
entries.text: A silver tabby, an old friend of Panther's, a little older than him. Knows things about him he'd rather she didn't say.

entries.title: Duchess
entries.text: The reigning Grand Circuit champion: large, white, very fluffy, gracious. More interested in boxes than trophies.

entries.title: The Grand Circuit
entries.text: One lap through the cardboard quarter, up the scratching-post ascent, over the cat-tree heights, along the toy boulevard and down the gardens to the finish under the Cat-a-tron.

entries.title: The sphere
entries.text: The last record: smooth and pale, almost unmarked until it is touched - then fine lines appear across it. It carries the same mark as the first piece, from the Moon.

entries.title: The archive chamber
entries.text: A round chamber beneath the lunar city, older than the mine: seven sockets round a central platform, walls for showing what it holds. It was built to bring the surviving records together - and to recognise a witness.

entries.title: The lunar network
entries.text: The city's old public network, locked behind Tunneler's restricted markings for years. Reopened, the Scree stations can hear each other, read their own history and run the city's controls themselves.
